knowledge_point.title: Finding Particular Solutions of Differential Equations by First Rearranging and Then Separating

question.:question/worked-solution:
We first find the general solution and then apply the given initial condition to find a particular solution.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-4(x - 1){y}^{2} & =4(x - 1) \\ 2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =4(x - 1){y}^{2}+4(x - 1) \\ 2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =4(x - 1)({y}^{2}+1) \\ \frac{2y}{{y}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}y & =4(x - 1)\,\text{d}x \\ \int \frac{2y}{{y}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}y & =\int 4(x - 1)\,\text{d}x \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({y}^{2}+1) & =2{(x - 1)}^{2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Exponentiating both sides, we find the general solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡({y}^{2}+1)} & ={e}^{2{(x - 1)}^{2}+C} \\ {y}^{2}+1 & =C{e}^{2{(x - 1)}^{2}} \\ y & =\sqrt{C{e}^{2{(x - 1)}^{2}}-1}\end{aligned}
$$

where we used that $y>0.$

We now apply the initial condition $y(1)=1$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(1) & =1 \\ \sqrt{C{e}^{2(0)^{2}}-1} & =1 \\ \sqrt{C-1} & =1 \\ C-1 & =1 \\ C & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the particular solution is

$$
y(x)=\sqrt{2{e}^{2{(x - 1)}^{2}}-1}.
$$
